phases.name: Warm-Up
phases.goal: Get the joints and muscles ready before loading the squat rack. 5 minutes — don't skip it.

tip.label: Purpose:
tip.text: Slow and controlled. 3 seconds down, pause at the bottom, drive up. This is mobility work — get the hips and knees tracking properly before adding load.

tip.label: Load:
tip.text: Use a light-to-moderate kettlebell. Elbows inside the knees at the bottom. This primes the quads and glutes before the barbell.

phases.name: Main Block — Squat Rack
phases.goal: The anchor of the session. Two barbell movements back to back — squats for quad and glute drive, RDL for posterior chain. Keep rest tight to stay in the 30-minute window.

tip.label: Cue:
tip.text: Chest up, knees tracking over toes, drive through the whole foot. Hit parallel or below on every rep — partial reps don't count.

tip.label: 3s eccentric:
tip.text: Take 3 seconds on the way down. Feel the hamstring stretch at the bottom before driving the hips forward. Keep the bar close to the legs the whole way.

phases.name: Dumbbell Burnout
phases.goal: Two dumbbell movements done back to back as a superset. No rest between exercises — rest 45 seconds after both. Finish the legs off completely.

tip.label: Superset:
tip.text: Step back — not forward — to reduce knee strain. Keep the front shin vertical. Go straight into the KB swings when done.

tip.label: Drive:
tip.text: Hinge at the hips — this is not a squat. Snap the hips forward to drive the bell. At 30 minutes this will be hard — push through the last few reps.

cards.title: Static Stretching — 4 min
cards.desc: Hip flexors, quads, hamstrings, glutes. Hold each 30–40 seconds. You've got a squat rack at home — use it for a supported pigeon stretch on the bench.

cards.title: Protein Window
cards.desc: Hit protein within 30–45 min. Short sessions still break down muscle — recovery nutrition matters just as much.
